title: Elysium demo: corridor survey and replanning near the InSight lander
summary: The drone surveys an uncertain corridor, finds a scarp, the first route is invalidated and the astronaut is replanned around it, reaches goal B and returns to base.
disclaimer: Terrain: NASA/USGS InSight HiRISE/CTX/HRSC DEM mosaic crop centred on the InSight lander (real, provisional, 8 m display grid from a 20 m source). InSight is a lander: no rover stops exist here. Mission, budgets and the corridor scarp are simulated or synthetic; POIs C and D are fictitious. Rover (1 m/s) and drone (4 m/s, 40 m up) motion is simulated; the rover is faster than real hardware (Perseverance about 4.2 cm/s), the drone below the Ingenuity top speed (about 5 m/s, flown at 10-24 m). Not EVA-certified limits, not a planner output.

ai_disclosure.scope: Fixture generator script and replay fixture structure; the simulated mission, routes and events are generated data, not observations.
ai_disclosure.observational_data: Only the terrain heights come from NASA/USGS data; everything else here is simulated.

Product page https://trek.nasa.gov/mars/. Native resolution 20 m. Not verified here: NASA planetary data served by JPL Mars Trek, see the Trek product page for usage terms.

Crop: 950 x 425 cells of 8 m centred at 4.502 N, 135.623 E, bilinear resampling onto a local tangent ENU grid (east = R cos(lat) dlon, north = R dlat); 8 m cells from a coarser source: no resolution gain. PROVISIONAL, made by the frontend until the data owner delivers the processed package.
SYNTHETIC: a scarp was added to the hidden evaluator reference to create an adverse case. It does not exist in the NASA terrain data.
ILLUSTRATIVE: uncertainty (sigma), budgets, speeds and consumption rates are assumptions of a simulated mission.

Chosen by the demo generator with a published NASA criterion, not a NASA site: the 1 km x 1 km area with the gentlest ground of the NASA DEM that meets the civil-engineering slope criterion of NASA's 2015 human Exploration Zone rubric (slope under 10 degrees at the 1 km scale: 0.2 degrees; within 5 km of the landing site, here base A: 2.43 km). Mean 8 m slope 0.7 degrees, 0 % of cells above 10 degrees. The rubric's ~50 km2 area and sparse rocks are not checked (crop too small, no rock-abundance data); water ice and hydrated minerals are not assessed (no such product imported).
